subsystems.name: Issuer and trust framework
subsystems.role: the body that vouches for a fact about you — your age, nationality or licence — and signs it.
parts: accredited issuers such as a government registry or bank

subsystems.name: Credential format and signatures
subsystems.role: lets the holder later reveal only part of what was signed, without breaking the signature.
parts: selective-disclosure schemes such as BBS+ signatures or SD-JWT

subsystems.name: Holder wallet
subsystems.role: keeps credentials on the user's own device and generates the proof only with their consent.

subsystems.name: Proof system and circuits
subsystems.role: turns the claim into a tiny proof that reveals nothing else.

subsystems.name: Verifier
subsystems.role: the relying party checks the proof in milliseconds and binds it to the current request.

subsystems.name: Revocation and status service
subsystems.role: prevents revoked or already-used credentials from working again.

buildSteps.title: Define the claim and the trust model
buildSteps.detail: Decide precisely what must be proved ('age is over 18', 'resident in this country'), who is allowed to sign it, and what the verifier is entitled to learn.

buildSteps.title: Issue a signed credential
buildSteps.detail: The issuer signs the user's attributes with a key that supports selective disclosure — for example a BBS+ signature or a salted SD-JWT — and hands the credential to the user's wallet.

buildSteps.title: Encode the claim as a circuit
buildSteps.detail: The verification logic is written as arithmetic constraints: the computation the proof must attest to, including hidden inputs for the secret attributes.

buildSteps.title: Set up the keys
buildSteps.detail: Systems like Groth16 need a one-time trusted setup per circuit, whose ceremony must be witnessed and destroyed afterwards; PLONK-style systems use a universal setup and STARKs need none at all.

buildSteps.title: Generate the witness and proof
buildSteps.detail: The wallet supplies the hidden values plus randomness, runs the prover on the phone or a server, and produces a short proof and a one-time nullifier.

buildSteps.title: Verify and bind the proof
buildSteps.detail: The relying party runs the verification key against the proof, checks a fresh session nonce so an old proof cannot be replayed, and reads the one public bit it asked for.

buildSteps.title: Wire in revocation
buildSteps.detail: The verifier checks a status list or accumulator, and records the nullifier so the same credential cannot be presented twice for the same entitlement.

buildSteps.title: Audit and operate
buildSteps.detail: The circuits, the setup ceremony and the wallet's randomness handling are audited; issuers rotate keys and publish status updates for the life of the system.

prerequisites.why: Groth16, PLONK and STARKs make proofs small and fast enough to verify on an ordinary server.
standards such as W3C Verifiable Credentials and SD-JWT with BBS+ are settled but unevenly deployed.

prerequisites.tech: Secure wallets in phones and browsers
prerequisites.why: the secret attributes and signing keys must stay on hardware the user controls.
without status checks and nullifiers a stolen or spent credential still works.
a verifier has to know which keys belong to a legitimate authority before believing any proof.

pathway.milestone: zero-knowledge proofs in production since Zcash in 2016 and now in zk-rollups verifying millions of proofs
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the cryptography works at scale, even though identity use is still mostly pilots.

pathway.milestone: EU Digital Identity Wallet under eIDAS 2.0, with member states required to offer wallets to residents during 2026
pathway.unlocks: hundreds of millions of people holding government-backed credentials that can prove a fact without handing over the document.

pathway.milestone: reusable KYC and age checks across unrelated services
pathway.unlocks: one verified credential instead of the same passport scan sent to dozens of companies.

pathway.milestone: general anonymous credentials, plus post-quantum and transparent proof systems
pathway.unlocks: everyday proofs about income, qualifications or entitlements with no central party seeing the underlying data.
